fiscal_year_note: NON-CALENDAR fiscal year: 52/53-week year ended September 27, 2025. Prior year ended September 28, 2024. Comparisons against calendar-year peers are not period-aligned.

accrued_amount.note: Apple does not quantify its legal accrual in the contingencies note.

reasonably_possible_loss_in_excess_of_ac.note: Apple affirmatively states there was NOT at least a reasonable possibility of a material loss, or a material loss greater than a recorded accrual. The correct extracted answer is 'no reasonably possible material loss asserted' — not a dollar amount and not 'not disclosed'.

legal_contingencies.verbatim_quote: The Company is subject to various legal proceedings and claims that have arisen in the ordinary course of business and that have not been fully resolved. The outcome of litigation is inherently uncertain. In the opinion of management, there was not at least a reasonable possibility the Company may have incurred a material loss, or a material loss greater than a recorded accrual, concerning loss contingencies for asserted legal and other claims.

individual_matters.note: The EU State Aid Decision is discussed in the TAX note (see income_taxes), not as a legal loss contingency.

legal_contingencies.why_hard: CONFLATION TRAP: the only occurrences of 'reasonably possible' with a dollar figure in Apple's filing are in the INCOME TAX note ($6 billion possible UTB decrease, line 940), not the legal contingencies note. An extractor keying on 'reasonably possible' + nearest dollar amount will wrongly report $6 billion as a legal loss contingency.

reconciling_items.label: Corporate
reconciling_items.note: Holds all R&D ($34,550) and G&A ($8,077); no revenue is allocated to Corporate. Not a reportable segment.

traps: Apple's segments are GEOGRAPHIC, not product lines. Extractors often report iPhone/Mac/iPad/Wearables/Services (a product revenue disaggregation) as segments — those are not reportable segments.
Segment operating income does NOT sum to consolidated operating income: the $42,627M Corporate column (all R&D + G&A) must be subtracted.
Corporate has zero revenue but a large negative operating income — asymmetric across the two builds.
An MD&A-level geographic net sales table (lines 371-378) prints the same revenue figures interleaved with percent-change columns, which can be mis-parsed as amounts.
Fiscal year ends September 27, 2025, not December 31.

income_taxes.income_before_income_taxes_note: PRINTED DIRECTLY on the consolidated income statement (line 542) as 'Income before provision for income taxes | 132,729'. This happens to match exactly the value derived from the computed-expected-tax line (27,873 / 0.21 = 132,729). Cross-check: 20,719 / 132,729 = 15.61%, consistent with the recorded 15.6% ETR.
income_taxes.column_order_warning: Apple's income statement is DESCENDING (2025 | 2024 | 2023): 'Income before provision for income taxes | 132,729 | 123,485 | 113,736'. FY2025 is the FIRST column — the OPPOSITE of Amazon and Alphabet in this same dataset. Do not assume a single convention across filers.
income_taxes.reconciliation_presentation: dollars only (no percent column), three years (2025, 2024, 2023)

rate_reconciliation_fy2025.line: Impact of the State Aid Decision

unrecognized_tax_benefits.verbatim_quote: As of September 27, 2025, the total amount of gross unrecognized tax benefits was $23.2 billion, of which $10.6 billion, if recognized, would impact the Company's effective tax rate. As of September 28, 2024, the total amount of gross unrecognized tax benefits was $22.0 billion, of which $10.8 billion, if recognized, would have impacted the Company's effective tax rate.

reasonably_possible_decrease_next_12_mon.as_printed: could decrease as much as $6 billion in the next 12 months
reasonably_possible_decrease_next_12_mon.verbatim_quote: Although the timing of resolution or closure of examinations is not certain, the Company believes it is reasonably possible that its gross unrecognized tax benefits could decrease as much as $6 billion in the next 12 months.

traps: The $6 billion 'reasonably possible' figure belongs to the UTB note, NOT legal contingencies — see legal_contingencies.why_hard.
The rate reconciliation is in DOLLARS ONLY with no percent column; the 21% statutory rate and 15.6% ETR appear in a different, MD&A-level table (lines 454-458).
The State Aid Decision swings from +10,246 (FY2024) to -486 (FY2025) — grabbing the wrong year column produces a wildly wrong reconciliation.
$23.2B gross UTB vs $10.6B ETR-affecting: reporting the gross figure as ETR-affecting is a ~2.2x error.
The same $23.2B / $10.6B sentence is repeated in the auditor's critical-audit-matter section (line 1141), so a naive first-match grep may land in the audit report rather than the tax note.
